question.worked_solution:
We perform the multiplication under a single radical and then simplify the result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{16w}\cdot 3\sqrt{9{w}^{3}} & = \\ 3\sqrt{16w\cdot 9{w}^{3}} & = \\ 3\sqrt{144{w}^{4}} & = \\ 3\sqrt{(12{w}^{2})^{2}} & = \\ 3|12{w}^{2}| & = \\ 3\cdot |12|\cdot |{w}^{2}| & = \\ 3\cdot 12\cdot |{w}^{2}| & = \\ 36\cdot |{w}^{2}|\end{aligned}
$$

A squared number is always positive or zero, and the absolute value of any positive (or zero) number is itself, so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}36\cdot |{w}^{2}| & =36{w}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
